metadata.title: Kenyon Sadiq Still Worth a Roster Spot After Week 4 Dud
metadata.description: New York Jets rookie tight end Kenyon Sadiq has been a focal point of the team's passing attack, despite a quiet Week 4 performance in the 23-12 loss to the Chicago Bears. In four games to start his NFL career, Sadiq has hauled in 12 of 18 targets for 143 yards and two touchdowns, averaging 8.2 half-PPR fantasy points per game. With Mason Taylor (thumb) inactive, Sadiq played 22 of 32 snaps (69%), ran 12 of 18 routes (67%), and led the team in targets (4). With the Jets dominated by the Bears in Week 4, it was nearly impossible for any player to produce with only 32 offensive snaps. With no timetable for Taylor's return, Sadiq will remain a focal point in New York's offense and should be rostered in all formats despite the tough outing.

metadata.title: Kenyon Sadiq held without a catch in Week 4 loss
metadata.description: Kenyon Sadiq was unable to catch any of his four targets in a 23-12 loss to the Bears in Week 4.
metadata.analysis: Sadiq was dealing with a back injury throughout the week but he was ultimately able to suit up vs. Chicago. He tied for the team lead in targets but was unable to do anything with them on a rough day for the New York passing offense. He now has 12 catches for 143 yards and one touchdown through four games. Sadiq will look to bounce back as a low-end TE1 in Week 5 against the Browns.

metadata.title: Kenyon Sadiq is Blanked in Week 4
metadata.description: New York Jets tight end Kenyon Sadiq was unable to carry his momentum from Week 3 into this weekend. The rookie tight end was held without a catch on four targets during the loss to the Chicago Bears. He was dealing with a back issue coming into this game, so that might've been part of the reason. The Jets only possessed the ball for 17 minutes in this game, so they didn't have a ton of time to do anything on offense. Sadiq tied wide receiver Garrett Wilson for the team lead in targets with four. This game was a dud, but overall, Sadiq has been a decent asset early on. He should be considered a low-end TE1 for the Week 5 matchup against the Cleveland Browns.

metadata.title: Kenyon Sadiq - Held catchless by Bears
metadata.description: Sadiq (back) didn't catch any of his four targets in Sunday's 23-12 loss to the Bears.
metadata.analysis: Sadiq played through a questionable tag and tied Garrett Wilson for the team lead in targets, but the rookie first-round pick failed to record a catch as Geno Smith completed only eight passes. The Jets' banged-up offense will try to bounce back when they return home for Week 5 against the Browns. Sadiq had 105 receiving yards and a touchdown in Week 3 against the Lions but has recorded only 38 receiving yards across the other three outings of his young NFL career.

metadata.title: Kenyon Sadiq (back) officially active for Week 4
metadata.description: Jets TE Kenyon Sadiq (back) is officially active for a Week 4 matchup with the Bears.
metadata.analysis: Sadiq was limited in each practice session this week but has been cleared to play Sunday. The rookie should see plenty of opportunities with WR Adonai Mitchell and RB Breece Hall both inactive Sunday.

metadata.title: Kenyon Sadiq - Active for Week 4
metadata.description: Sadiq (back) is listed as active for Sunday's game against the Bears.
metadata.analysis: A back injury led to Sadiq being limited at practice from Wednesday through Friday, but it will not prevent him from suiting up for Week 4. It's unclear how close Sadiq is to 100 percent, but he is coming off a game in which he racked up seven receptions, 105 yards and a score on eight targets, and he could be busy again with fellow pass catchers Adonai Mitchell (finger), Mason Taylor (thumb) and Omar Cooper (ankle) all unavailable Sunday.

metadata.title: Kenyon Sadiq Active for Week 4 Against Bears
metadata.description: New York Jets tight end Kenyon Sadiq (back) is officially active for Sunday's Week 4 contest against the Chicago Bears. Sadiq had been listed as questionable after practicing in a limited capacity all week long. Having the rookie available on Sunday is great news for the Jets, who already ruled out fellow tight end Mason Taylor (thumb) earlier in the week. Sadiq will continue to operate as New York's No. 1 tight end, looking to build off last week's fantastic stat line of seven catches, 105 yards, and one touchdown. That level of volume and productivity makes Sadiq an intriguing TE1 option in fantasy football this week. However, we acknowledge that his floor will be on the lower side as long as Geno Smith is his quarterback.

metadata.title: Kenyon Sadiq Questionable but Still Has TE1 Appeal
metadata.description: New York Jets tight end Kenyon Sadiq (back) is questionable after being limited in all three practices this week. If he's active, though, the setup is still appealing. Mason Taylor (thumb) and Adonai Mitchell (finger) have both been ruled out, two absences that helped open the door for Sadiq's seven-catch, 105-yard, one-touchdown breakout against Detroit. He did that on eight targets and now has 12 receptions for 143 yards through three games. There is some snap-count caution here because Sadiq played 57% of the offensive snaps last week, and the back issue adds another layer of uncertainty. RotoBaller's Saturday update has him at TE10. Fantasy managers should have a backup plan available Sunday morning, but Sadiq is a legitimate TE1 if the Jets clear him to play.

metadata.title: Kenyon Sadiq (back) questionable to play Sunday
metadata.description: Kenyon Sadiq (back) is questionable to play in Sunday's game against the Chicago Bears.
metadata.analysis: The rookie had a breakout performance in Week 3, but his momentum may be halted by an injury, as he is now questionable to play ahead of Sunday's game against the Bears. If he's ruled out, look for veteran Jeremy Ruckert to serve as the team's TE1 with Mason Taylor (thumb) already ruled out for the Jets.

metadata.title: Kenyon Sadiq - Listed questionable for Sunday
metadata.description: Sadiq (back) is questionable for Sunday's game against the Bears.
metadata.analysis: After logging limited practices earlier in the week, Sadiq now carries a questionable tag into Week 4. With Mason Taylor (thumb) already ruled out against Chicago, Sadiq's status bears monitoring over the next 48 hours. If he's cleared to play, the rookie tight end should once again have a significant pass-catching role after posting his first career 100-yard receiving game with a touchdown last Sunday against the Lions.

metadata.title: Kenyon Sadiq Questionable Against Bears
metadata.description: New York Jets tight end Kenyon Sadiq (back) is questionable for Sunday's game against the Chicago Bears. Sadiq was limited Wednesday and Thursday after his breakout performance in Week 3, when he caught seven of eight targets for 105 yards and a touchdown against Detroit. That brought him to 12 receptions for 143 yards through his first three NFL games. There should still be plenty available to him if he plays. Tight end Mason Taylor and wide receiver Adonai Mitchell have already been ruled out, leaving the Jets short on pass catchers once again. RotoBaller has Sadiq at TE9 for Week 4 after last week's jump in usage. His questionable tag makes it worth having another tight end available Sunday morning, but Sadiq belongs in fantasy lineups if he gets the green light against Chicago.

metadata.title: Kenyon Sadiq - Another limited practice Thursday
metadata.description: Sadiq (back) remained limited at practice Thursday.
metadata.analysis: Sadiq has been limited in each of the Jets' first two practices leading up to Sunday's game against the Bears. The rookie tight end took a hard landing on a diving catch that resulted in the first receiving touchdown of his NFL career in the Week 3 loss to the Lions, so his back injury may be connected to that play. Sadiq will have one more chance to increase his practice participation level Friday before the Jets release their Week 4 injury statuses.

metadata.title: Kenyon Sadiq (back) limited in practice Thursday
metadata.description: Kenyon Sadiq remained limited in practice on Thursday.
metadata.analysis: Sadiq has logged back-to-back limited practices. He is on track to be good to go on Sunday.

metadata.title: Kenyon Sadiq - Dealing with back issue
metadata.description: Sadiq was limited at Wednesday's practice due to a back injury.
metadata.analysis: Meanwhile, fellow TE Jeremy Ruckert (knee) also was limited, while Mason Taylor (thumb) didn't practice. In Taylor's absence this past Sunday at Detroit, Sadiq, a rookie first-round pick, broke out with seven catches (on eight targets) for 105 yards and one touchdown. Another hefty workload could be on tap for Sadiq in Week 5 at Chicago if Taylor remains sidelined and Ruckert also is less than 100 percent. First, though, the statuses of the three players will continue to be watched to get a sense of the overall situation.

metadata.title: Kenyon Sadiq Limited With Back Injury on Wednesday
metadata.description: New York Jets rookie first-round tight end Kenyon Sadiq (back) is dealing with a back injury and was listed as a limited participant in practice on Wednesday. The Jets' tight end group is a bit banged up going into their Week 4 road contest against the Chicago Bears, with Jeremy Ruckert (knee) limited and Mason Taylor (thumb) missing another practice. Taylor did not play in last week's loss to the Detroit Lions, and Sadiq took advantage, catching seven of his eight targets for a season-high 105 yards and his first receiving touchdown of his career. It looks like Taylor could miss another game, but even when he returns, the 21-year-old Sadiq is expected to be the better downfield pass-catching option for the Jets at the position. Sadiq had only five catches for 38 yards in his first two NFL games, but he did manage to find the end zone on a three-yard rush. Sadiq could have TE1 upside for a second straight week in Week 4 if he is active and both Taylor and receiver Adonai Mitchell (finger) miss another game.

metadata.title: Kenyon Sadiq to be limited in practice Wednesday
metadata.description: Kenyon Sadiq will be limited in practice on Wednesday.
metadata.analysis: Sadiq is coming off a career best performance this past week. He should remain in a bigger role if Adonai Mitchell (finger) misses another game.

metadata.title: Kenyon Sadiq - Limited in Wednesday's practice
metadata.description: Sadiq was limited Wednesday, Zack Rosenblatt of The Athletic reports.
metadata.analysis: With no injury detail provided, this is mainly a midweek practice update for the Jets' tight end. Sadiq's participation level will be worth monitoring later in the week for any clearer indication of his status.

metadata.title: Kenyon Sadiq Emerges As Strong Waiver-Wire Option in Week 4
metadata.description: New York Jets rookie tight end Kenyon Sadiq caught seven of eight passes for 105 yards and a touchdown in the 31-24 loss to the Detroit Lions. With wide receiver Adonai Mitchell (finger) and tight end Mason Taylor (thumb) inactive, Sadiq had a breakout game, being one of two tight ends to have over 100 yards in Week 3. However, he played only 57% of the snaps and ran 58% of the routes, while Jelani Woods and Jeremy Ruckert also saw significant roles. If Mitchell or Taylor return next week against the Chicago Bears, Sadiq could see fewer targets, but he looked special and will be difficult to keep off the field. Sadiq should be a strong waiver-wire option as he looks to carry this momentum into Week 4.

metadata.title: Kenyon Sadiq finds the end zone in Week 3 loss
metadata.description: Kenyon Sadiq caught 7-of-8 targets for 105 yards and a touchdown in a 31-24 loss to the Jets.
metadata.analysis: Sadiq caught his first NFL touchdown pass on a great catch in the second quarter as he stretched out to haul in the pass in the end zone. The rookie tight end was second on the team in receptions, yards, and targets, just behind Garrett Wilson. Sadiq and the Jets will take on the Bears on the road in Week 4.

metadata.title: Kenyon Sadiq - Catches first TD pass
metadata.description: Sadiq caught seven of eight passes for 105 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 31-24 loss to the Lions.
metadata.analysis: The rookie tight end made a spectacular play to haul in his first career TD reception in the second quarter, leaping from about the five-yard line and stretching out the full length of his 6-foot-3 frame to bring in a 24-yard pass from Geno Smith. Sadiq is very quickly making an impact with his athleticism, and through his first three NFL games he's compiled a 12-143-1 line on 14 targets while adding a three-yard score on his only carry. He'll look to continue building chemistry with Smith in a Week 4 road trip to Chicago.

metadata.title: Rookie Kenyon Sadiq Breaks Out Versus Lions
metadata.description: New York Jets rookie first-round tight end Kenyon Sadiq delivered career highs with eight targets, seven receptions, 105 receiving yards, and his first career receiving touchdown in a 31-24 loss to the Detroit Lions in Week 3. He played 38 offensive snaps, which was the most among tight ends for New York. This was just the third career game for the rookie, so there is plenty of time for Sadiq to best those numbers in the future as well. Sadiq entered Sunday's game with five receptions for 38 yards, and one rushing attempt for a three-yard touchdown. Currently rostered in just 18% of Yahoo leagues, Sadiq will likely be a popular waiver wire target ahead of a Week 4 matchup with the Chicago Bears. He remains a strong dynasty player.

metadata.title: Kenyon Sadiq Gets a Bigger Opportunity in Week 3
metadata.description: New York Jets tight end Kenyon Sadiq caught two of three targets for 17 yards against Green Bay after recording three receptions for 21 yards and a rushing touchdown in his NFL debut. His Week 3 opportunity is more interesting now that Mason Taylor has officially been ruled out with a thumb injury. Taylor did not practice at all this week, leaving Sadiq and Jeremy Ruckert to handle the available tight-end work. Detroit gave up seven catches for 95 yards and a touchdown to Dalton Kincaid last Thursday, although Sadiq has not shown anything close to that kind of receiving role yet. RotoBaller ranks him as the TE32 for Week 3. He remains a risky play in normal leagues, but Taylor's absence gives Sadiq his clearest path yet to additional routes and targets.

metadata.title: Kenyon Sadiq Could See More Work in Week 3
metadata.description: New York Jets tight end Kenyon Sadiq has not done enough yet to trust in a fantasy lineup, but his path to more work may be opening up. The rookie caught two passes for 17 yards against Green Bay after posting three catches for 21 yards and a three-yard rushing touchdown in Week 1. He now has five receptions for 38 yards through two games. Mason Taylor (thumb) left Sunday's loss late, and his Week 3 status is still unclear, which could push Sadiq into a larger role against Detroit. New York spent the 16th overall pick on Sadiq, and his offseason was interrupted by hernia surgery before he later suffered a setback in training camp. RotoBaller has him 40th overall on its Week 3 waiver board and recommends him in 14-team leagues. That feels like the right range. Sadiq is not a streamer yet, but deeper-league managers can stash him now in case the opportunity grows faster than expected.

metadata.title: Kenyon Sadiq - Two snags in loss
metadata.description: Sadiq caught two of three targets for 17 yards during Sunday's 20-17 overtime loss to the Packers.
metadata.analysis: Sadiq was only on the field for 27 of the team's 74 offensive snaps, but he was able to record multiple catches for the second game in a row to open his career. The most notable development of the game for Sadiq came in the second half when starting tight end Mason Taylor suffered a thumb injury. If Taylor is unavailable for Week 3, Sadiq would stand to operate as the Jets' unquestioned top option at tight end against the Lions' porous secondary.

metadata.title: Kenyon Sadiq catches two passes in Week 2
metadata.description: Kenyon Sadiq caught two of his three targets for 17 yards in the Jets' 20-17 loss to the Green Bay Packers in Week 2.
metadata.analysis: Sadiq fell back to earth after an impactful Week 1 performance, finishing with less than three receptions in the losing effort. The tight end remains one of many unproven pass-catching options as part of a revamped Jets passing attack ahead of a Week 3 contest against the Detroit Lions.

metadata.title: Kenyon Sadiq Needs More Than his Week 1 Touchdown
metadata.description: New York Jets rookie first-round tight end Kenyon Sadiq found a fun way to score his first NFL touchdown, taking an end-around three yards into the end zone on the Jets' opening drive. He also caught all three of his targets for 21 yards. The bigger issue is how crowded the position remains. New York used plenty of heavy tight-end personnel against Tennessee, and Sadiq was sharing the field and opportunities with Mason Taylor, Jeremy Ruckert and Jelani Woods. That can keep him involved without necessarily turning into a useful weekly target total. Green Bay allowed T.J. Hockenson to score last week, but Sadiq is still only TE35 in RotoBaller's Week 2 rankings. The touchdown was encouraging. Three targets are not enough yet to make him a standard-league starter.

metadata.title: Kenyon Sadiq a Waiver Priority After Scoring First Career Touchdown
metadata.description: New York Jets rookie first-round tight end Kenyon Sadiq missed valuable time during training camp this summer following a setback after hernia surgery, but he was active in the Week 1 season-opening win on Sunday over the Tennessee Titans and had an impact on offense. Sadiq caught all three of his targets in his NFL debut for 21 yards and also scored a three-yard rushing touchdown on his only carry of the game. The Jets acknowledged that they would ease Sadiq into the fold early in his first NFL season, which was the case, as he played 42% of the offensive snaps, which was behind both Mason Taylor and Jeremy Ruckert. However, Taylor had just two catches for minus-two yards, and Ruckert caught his only target for a four-yard gain against Tennessee. The 21-year-old from Oregon is a physical specimen with versatility and should only continue to be more involved in the Jets' downfield passing attack as the season goes, making him a priority waiver-wire pickup, even in single-TE leagues. Sadiq has much more short- and long-term fantasy upside than Taylor.

metadata.title: Kenyon Sadiq - Creeps into No. 1 TE conversation
metadata.description: Sadiq caught all three of his targets for 31 yards in Sunday's 23-10 win over the Titans. He added one rush for a three-yard touchdown.
metadata.analysis: Sadiq caught one more pass than current listed No. 1 tight end Mason Taylor, and his 31 yards dwarfed Taylor's negative two. The first-round rookie also showcased his versatility when he scored a three-yard rushing touchdown on an end-around early in the first quarter. Sadiq could eventually take over as the primary big-bodied option for the Jets now that he is fully healthy and has experienced the NFL regular season.

metadata.title: Kenyon Sadiq rushes for TD in Week 1
metadata.description: Kenyon Sadiq caught all three of his targets for 21 yards and added a three-yard rushing touchdown in a 23-10 win over the Titans in Week 2.
metadata.analysis: Sadiq turned in a quiet outing in the passing attack but he scored the Jets' first TD of the season on his three-yard carry in the first quarter. The team's willingness to use the first-round rookie in the running game is an encouraging development for his fantasy value moving forward. Sadiq will be a solid TE2 in Week 2 against the Packers.

metadata.title: Kenyon Sadiq (groin) without injury designation for Sunday
metadata.description: Kenyon Sadiq (groin) is without an injury designation for Sunday's game against the Tennessee Titans.
metadata.analysis: The rookie will be available to make his NFL debut on Sunday. He is fully over his groin injury at this point and should have no major limitations in this matchup against the Titans. Fantasy managers shouldn't have high expectations for him in this matchup, however.

metadata.title: Kenyon Sadiq "Good to Go" in Week 1
metadata.description: New York Jets rookie tight end Kenyon Sadiq (groin) is "good to go" for his team's season opener against the Tennessee Titans on Sunday, per ESPN's Adam Schefter. Sadiq missed significant time throughout the summer due to complications from an offseason hernia surgery. However, he was reportedly heavily involved in the Jets' offense when healthy during training camp, and he was able to log full practices throughout this week leading into Week 1. The 16th overall pick in the 2026 NFL Draft, Sadiq recorded 51 catches for 560 yards and eight touchdowns across 14 games with the University of Oregon in 2025. The 21-year-old graded out at the Draft Combine as an elite athlete for the tight end position, which should allow the Jets to get him the ball in a variety of ways this season. Given his injury issues this summer, Sadiq may not hit the ground running immediately as a rookie. Still, he's a worthy stash candidate in deeper fantasy leagues for his season-long upside.

metadata.title: Kenyon Sadiq Has Integrated Himself into the Offense
metadata.description: New York Jets rookie tight end Kenyon Sadiq (groin) was an early training camp standout before complications related to offseason hernia surgery caused him to miss significant time, but he was a full participant during Wednesday's practice, and offensive coordinator Frank Reich told reporters on Thursday that he has integrated himself well into the offense. Sadiq was the 16th overall pick in the 2026 NFL Draft after turning in a historic Combine performance, and he finds himself in a Jets offense well-equipped to take advantage of his dynamic skill set. Reich's offenses have historically featured the tight end position, and the Jets are in need of a secondary pass-catching option behind Garrett Wilson, who led the team with 395 receiving yards in 2025 despite missing 10 games. With Sadiq's injury causing him to go undrafted in many redraft leagues, he profiles as a potential waiver add before Sunday's season opener against the Titans.
